title: Propulsion Mechanisms — Spacetime Engineering
data_note: Model-dependent quantities for selected spacetime-engineering calculations. Casimir values refer to an ideal parallel-plate calculation; Pfenning-Ford values refer to a specific Alcubierre profile. They must not be combined into a geometry-independent technology-gap ratio.

statistics.unit: m (approximately 100 Planck lengths for v_b near c)
statistics.source: Pfenning, M. J. & Ford, L. H. (1997). The unphysical nature of 'Warp Drive'. Classical and Quantum Gravity, 14(7), 1743-1751. https://doi.org/10.1088/0264-9381/14/7/011
statistics.context: For their selected sampling assumptions and a bubble speed of order c, Pfenning and Ford obtained Delta <= 10^2 v_b L_P, i.e. order 1e-33 m. The paper describes a few hundred Planck lengths in its illustrative discussion. This is a model-dependent quantum-inequality bound, not a universal wall thickness or a fabrication specification. The 10^2 coefficient follows from P&F's sampling-time choice alpha = 1/10 (their eq. 22-23).
statistics.verification_note: Source and order-of-magnitude calculation checked. The theoretical derivation is conditional on the chosen Alcubierre profile, sampling time, velocity, and semiclassical assumptions; it is not an empirical measurement.

statistics.metric: Casimir negative energy density at 100 nm separation
statistics.source: Casimir, H. B. G. (1948). On the attraction between two perfectly conducting plates. Proceedings of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences, 51, 793-795. https://www.dwc.knaw.nl/DL/publications/PU00018547.pdf; Lamoreaux, S. K. (1997). Demonstration of the Casimir Force in the 0.6 to 6 Micrometer Range. https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.78.5
statistics.context: For ideal perfectly conducting parallel plates, u = -pi^2 hbar c / (720 a^4). At a = 100 nm this evaluates to -4.33375257 J/m^3. Real plates require geometry, conductivity, roughness, and temperature corrections. Casimir-force measurements validate boundary-dependent vacuum stress but do not directly create a stockpileable negative-energy material.
statistics.verification_note: Ideal-plate formula independently recalculated with hbar = 1.054571817e-34 J s and c = 299792458 m/s. The listed number is a theoretical ideal-geometry value, not Lamoreaux's measured density at 100 nm.

statistics.metric: Pfenning-Ford 100 m bubble total negative mass-equivalent
statistics.unit: kg mass-equivalent per unit v_b (v_b in units of c)
statistics.source: Pfenning, M. J. & Ford, L. H. (1997). The unphysical nature of 'Warp Drive'. Classical and Quantum Gravity, 14(7), 1743-1751. https://doi.org/10.1088/0264-9381/14/7/011
statistics.context: For the paper's specific 100 m-radius Alcubierre example after imposing its quantum-inequality wall bound, the integrated negative energy is approximately -6.2e65 g = -6.2e62 kg in mass-equivalent terms, or about -5.6e79 J. This is not a universal warp-drive requirement and must not be mixed with unrelated Jupiter-mass estimates or assumed uniform shell densities. P&F eq. (29): E <= -6.2e65 v_b g; the magnitude scales linearly with v_b, and the stored value assumes v_b = 1.
statistics.verification_note: Value and gram-to-kilogram conversion checked against Pfenning and Ford. It is an integrated, model-dependent negative mass-equivalent, not an energy-density measurement.

statistics.source: Assessment based on s03-001 through s03-003 and their incompatible geometries and dimensions.
statistics.context: No defensible universal ratio exists. The ideal Casimir value is a local energy density for a specified plate geometry, whereas Pfenning-Ford report an integrated mass-equivalent for a specified warp profile. A ratio requires a matched target metric, local stress-energy distribution, wall profile, speed, and averaging prescription.
statistics.verification_note: The prior 1e68 value divided an incorrect 100 nm Casimir number by an unsupported, geometry-mismatched warp density. It has been removed rather than replaced with another universal factor.
